unreg:league_tie_and_long_kick_counts.reviewer: independent-NFL (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:league_tie_and_long_kick_counts.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading the record: (1) exposure: set of games left in the window (272-game season; Week 2 slate of 16, which has no byes) plus the banked count as of the as-of time; (2) per-game tie = P(level after 60 min) x P(level after 10-minute OT under the rule era), roughly 0.3 percent per game; season ties are a Poisson-binomial sum; (3) 60+ makes = attempts (end-of-half and end-of-game hazard by coach, kicker ceiling, altitude, roof, wind, K-ball era) x make probability falling steeply past 55 yards, summed over kickers, with a few kickers and venues dominating; (4) settlement: the official distance definition, free-kick FGs, postponed games, rungs as nested thresholds. Required: schedule/banked-count dataset, own margin lattice, OT rule-era model, kick-level play-by-play with distance, kicker ceiling data. The record matches on stages and inputs but differs on: banked-count/exposure inputs are not attached to the archetype, the attempt hazard input outputs 65+ yard attempts, and some contract facts are stated as established that the text does not give. The Kalshi API confirms the three rules texts and shows KXNFLTIES rungs 2/3/4 and KXNFL60YARDFGS rungs 6/8/16, which the record does not mention.

findings.text: Stages s1 and s5 stage nfl.season_to_date_pace and nfl.games_played_dist, but neither is in the archetype's input list, so the exposure and banked-count stage has no attached input. Their catalog definitions are player-season accrual and injury-attrition inputs, not league-window counts. Nothing defines banked ties or banked 60+ makes by as-of timestamp, games remaining or the treatment of unplayed games. Needs a defined window-exposure input (schedule remaining, banked count, as-of rule) attached to the archetype, or the stage ids replaced with ones it carries.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: new input nfl.league_window_banked_count_and_exposure (banked count, games remaining, as-of rule, unplayed flag) attached and staged in s1/s5; the player-level accrual inputs were removed from stages and feeds.

findings.text: The primary input nfl.long_fg_end_of_half_attempt_hazard (stage s3) is defined for 65+ yard attempts: its mechanism is a 65+ attempt beating a Hail Mary or punt, and its output is 'expected 65+, 68+, 70+ yard attempts'. The contract counts made kicks of 60 yards or more, and the record's own make curve (0.3-0.5 at 60-63 yards) puts most expected makes at 60-64 yards, which this input does not output. The attempt side of attempts x make is therefore not defined for the contract threshold. Needs a 60+ attempt hazard by distance band.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.fg_attempt_hazard_by_distance_band_60plus (60-64, 65-69, 70+) attached, staged in s3, filter corrected to yardline_100 43-62 so 60 and 61 yard attempts are included; verified in merged catalog.

findings.text: rules_evidence 'establishes' text for KXNFLTIES says a postponed game still counts when played within the season, and KXNFLWEEKTIE says a tie after overtime is the only qualifying result. Neither is in the sampled text, and the record's own settlement_definition and u1 say postponement is unstated. s1 and s5 then treat it as an assumption. Inference is presented as verified from rules text.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: the three rules_evidence 'establishes' lines were rewritten to state only what the sampled text gives and say postponement and unplayed games are unstated.

findings.text: Era and base-rate claims are uncited: the 2025 ball-preparation rule 'followed by a jump in 60+ makes' (nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era), the 2025 both-possess 10-minute regular-season overtime, season tie mean 0.5-1.5, 60+ make mean 3-8, 10-25 attempts a season. I could not verify them here. The strikes (4+ ties, 8+ makes) are only meaningful against these, so a tie and 60+ make history by season from official game books or nflverse would resolve them.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: base rates, the 2025 ball-preparation effect and the overtime rule are now declared unsourced in u5 and marked placeholders in stages; I corroborated both rule changes by secondary search only.

findings.text: Internal arithmetic and facts: s3 gives 0.03-0.08 attempts per team-game, which over 544 team-games is 16-44 attempts, but the same stage says 10-25 attempts a season. s1 says the weekly slate has 14-16 games depending on byes, but Week 2 has no byes (16 games). KXNFLWEEKTIE-26W2-Y is already finalized (opened 2026-09-17, result no), so the weekly contract has no live exposure now.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: the 0.03-0.08 per team-game versus 10-25 season arithmetic is withdrawn in s3, the Week 2 byes claim is hedged to 'to confirm', and the finalized weekly sample is noted.

findings.text: Contract mechanics missed: the live series are rung ladders (KXNFLTIES 2/3/4, KXNFL60YARDFGS 6/8/16), so the model must output a monotone nested distribution, and the record treats single strikes. nfl.kicking_ball_and_fg_rule_era says fair-catch free kicks are scored as field goals, yet no unresolved entry asks whether a made free-kick field goal of 60+ counts for KXNFL60YARDFGS, and u3 covers only kick-distance source.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: s5 and variants now state the N+ strikes are nested events needing a monotone distribution, and u4 asks whether a made free-kick field goal of 60+ counts.

findings.text: availability_news is marked COVERED by nfl.preseason_long_kick_evidence alone. Kicker signings, injuries and the few 60+ capable kickers' availability are the personnel driver of the count and have no input. Also nfl.weekly_slate_composition's catalog definition still says 'setting N for the argmax', text from another archetype.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: availability_news changed to GAP with u5 declaring kicker availability unmeasured, and the 'argmax' text removed from nfl.weekly_slate_composition rationale; verified in merged catalog.

unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials.reviewer: independent-NFL (Claude agent, agent verification, not human expert)
unreg:team_and_event_counting_specials.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading the record: per-game counts are opportunities x per-opportunity rate. Field goals = stalled drives in range x coach kick-or-go decision x make probability. Team sacks = opponent dropbacks (excluding two-point tries) x pressure x pressure-to-sack conversion, modified by QB availability and script. Yards = plays x yield per play with an explosive-play tail. Both-team conversions = attempts (coach policy by score path) x success. All overdispersed and score-path dependent, with overtime possibly counting. KXNFLNEXTINT is different: a survival probability over the games in a schedule window, 1 - product of per-game zero-interception chances, needing the game list, opposing quarterbacks and the issuance rule. Required inputs: opportunity counts, kicker and red-zone data, pressure and sack decomposition, own score-state model, decision policies, a schedule-window input. The record agrees on all of this. It differs in that the script input is market-centred, the window has no input of its own, stale tie, 60+ and first-down text survives, and primary labels disagree with the audit verdicts.

findings.text: nfl.script is staged in five of seven stages (s1, s3, s4, s5, s7) and two interactions but its catalog measurement still integrates over 'the distribution of game states implied by spread/total (Gaussian margin around spread)', a market-derived input. The record only says in the input_audit reason that the margin must come from own ratings; the input definition was not changed or replaced, so a market line is still smuggled in as an input. Replace with a definition over own-model margin distribution.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.script measurement rebased on market-free own-model margin and total distributions (nfl.model_team_points_mean, nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd); betting lines no longer used.

findings.text: KXNFLNEXTINT has a separate chain (stage s6 only; s2-s5 and s7 do not apply) and no input defines its window: the list of games after issuance and before Week 8, byes, issuance timestamp, opposing starting QB. The schedule slice is declared as a GAP only in the situational category note, and u6 covers only stakes, not the missing window input. 'After issuance' is not defined for a game already in progress at issuance, and this is not in unresolved. My view: the series should be its own archetype (team multi-game window hazard), not stay here; see gap audit.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: KXNFLNEXTINT re-filed to new archetype unreg:team_window_event_hazards with window input nfl.team_window_game_exposure and survival input; no NEXTINT stage remains in the counting record.

findings.text: Stale text from the former mixed record remains. The live nfl.ot_model why still says 'it bounds tie markets'; required_data history_needed says '5 for long field goals'; the retained nfl.streak_and_undefeated_hazard_path definition still carries banked 60+ yard FG and tie-count language; the nfl.kicker audit reason says it 'determine[s] long-field-goal counts'; the nfl.success_rate why is 'drives first downs' and an old interaction says 'raising first downs', though no first-down series is live. The reconcile log does not list these.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: stale tie, 60+ yard and first-down text removed from ot_model why, history_needed, kicker audit reason, success_rate why; streak input detached from this archetype.

findings.text: Roles contradict the audit: nfl.pace, nfl.success_rate and nfl.int_rate are carried as primary but audited KEEP_SECONDARY, and nfl.safety_risk is carried primary but audited WEAK with a generic why ('Safety and special-play event risk'). Roles were not updated.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: pace, success_rate carried secondary, safety_risk context, int_rate detached; roles now match input_audit verdicts in the merged catalog.

findings.text: nfl.penalties and nfl.officials_crew are carried (secondary), listed in required_data feeds_inputs, and staged in no stage, while officiating_rules is NOT_APPLICABLE. They are irrelevant inputs left attached; detach or stage them.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.penalties and nfl.officials_crew detached from the archetype and absent from required_data feeds_inputs; officiating_rules stays NOT_APPLICABLE.

findings.text: Interaction on two-point and fourth-down counts asserts that an expected blowout produces more trailing-team tries, 'reversing the usual close-game intuition', without evidence. The conversion counts are not linked to a score-path simulator (acknowledged in u1), and sampled both-team series are all one Super Bowl.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: the fourth-down x script interaction was rebuilt as a three-input hedged hypothesis (nfl.fourth_down_fg_decision_rate, nfl.script, nfl.coaching) stating no evidence is offered; the unsupported "reversing the usual close-game intuition" claim is gone from the merged record.

findings.text: Quoted base rates are uncited: FG mean 1.6 per team, sacks 2.3, interceptions 0.7, yards 330 +/- 80, safety 1 in 15-20 games, overtime in 6-8 percent of games. Sources (nflverse play-by-play per-team-game tables) were not checked here. The rules quotes are verbatim against contract_rules_sample.json; the overtime treatment is correctly marked unestablished.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: base rates relabelled unsourced placeholders in stage distributions s2-s6 and carried in u7; play-by-play values still unchecked (closure by disclosure, not by evidence).
